title: Office parsers synchronously inflate untrusted ZIP input without resource limits
reasoning: All parse entrypoints fully inflate user-supplied Office files synchronously and materialize every ZIP entry before validating the package. A compressed ZIP bomb or a package with many large entries can consume memory/CPU and freeze or crash the desktop app or add-in process. The feature's trust boundaries include filesystem and user input, so this is a concrete denial-of-service risk.
recommendation: Introduce a shared safe OOXML ZIP reader that enforces maximum input size, maximum entry count, maximum total uncompressed bytes, per-entry size limits, and an allowlist of required parts. Prefer inflating only needed XML parts and run heavy parsing off the UI thread where applicable.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: All linked tests build small in-memory ZIP fixtures and do not include oversized, highly-compressed, or high-entry-count packages.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a parser test that constructs a ZIP entry exceeding a configured uncompressed-size limit, plus a high-entry-count package, and assert the adapters reject them with a controlled error before returning a model.
minimumFixScope: Create and use a bounded unzip helper across packages/core/src/adapters/word/parse.ts, packages/core/src/adapters/excel/parse.ts, packages/core/src/adapters/powerpoint/parse.ts, and packages/core/src/adapters/metadata.ts; add adapter-level limit tests.
